name: Running in Beijing: How Pleasant Is This Street?
description:
Method replication: participants give their age and gender, then rate how pleasant running would feel at 10 random Beijing street views on five levels (Very bad, Bad, Not bad, Pleasant, Very pleasant); the images are not the paper's stimuli (54 newly fetched Baidu street views on roads around central Beijing parks, rivers and the Olympic area, facing along the road, cropped to remove the camera car).

Original study: Zhang, Song & Zhang (2022), Journal of Geographical Sciences 32(12), 2624–2640. Baidu street views were taken every 100 m along 153 running routes in central Beijing from the Runtastic app (8,260 valid points), facing the running direction. A Tencent questionnaire shared on social media showed each volunteer 10 random images from 101 points, rated on the five-level pleasure scale; 446 valid questionnaires gave 4,460 ratings. Scores by age and gender group were modelled against segmented landscape elements and landscape types.

Differences from the original study: (1) the authors' running routes are not public, so images come from roads near popular running places rather than recorded routes; (2) images face along the road in either direction rather than the recorded running direction.
author: Zhang, Song & Zhang
